How this grade was reached

This scan landed in the A band. The A+ band is not available at Level 1 and is drawn here so the scale is not mistaken for the whole range.

The grade is driven by the single worst finding, not by an average or a count — one critical exposure is one way in, and nine clean ports do not offset it. The first row that matches decides the result:

IfScoreGrade
any critical finding40F
else any high finding60C
else any medium finding78B
else nothing responded, or the scan was stopped early, or our own probes failed—N/A
else any low or info finding90A
else no exposure observed94A

A is the ceiling at this tier. A+ is reserved for an assessment that cryptographically verifies hardware attestation and fabric isolation, which needs access inside the hosts. A Level 1 scan cannot collect that evidence, so it does not award the grade that claims it — a clean result here is an A, and that is the best this tier has.

Note the order: a finding we did observe stands even if the scan did not finish, because an observed exposure is evidence either way. The reverse does not hold — an incomplete or unreached scan can never earn a clean grade, because absence of coverage is not absence of exposure.

Scope & method

This is an agentless, read-only Level 1 assessment run from outside the hosts. It observes which services are reachable, whether they require authentication, and their transport posture. It does not install software, does not require credentials, and cannot assess cross-tenant fabric isolation or hardware attestation — those need deeper tiers.

Every finding below is therefore recorded at evidence level observed: seen from outside the host, once, at the time of the scan. Nothing here claims a configuration was read, a signature verified, or hardware attested — those are higher levels, and this tier cannot reach them. What does differ between findings is how the service was identified, which each finding states on its own Evidence line: a service that answered on its own API is a stronger identification than one identified only by a root page any web server would answer.

Read-only assessment. Detection by observation, not exploitation. No customer payload — no model weights, prompts, training data, inference content, or object contents — was read, stored, or transmitted. Grade thresholds are provisional and will be revised as they are validated.
